sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 04.07.2017 at about 7.00 a.m. when the deceased Padurangappa was traveling in a Mahindra pick- up vehicle bearing registration No.KA-16-C-5285 and when he reached near Patrehall Village NH-4 road, Hiriyur Taluk, the said vehicle met with an accident with a lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-30-BB-2878 because of which, the said Padurangappa expired.
The accident happened due NC: 2023:KHC:33686 to rash and negligent driving of the lorry, which was duly insured with respondent no.2- Insurance Company.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.12,00,000/-
along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners who are wife and children of the deceased have preferred this appeal.
4. The accident occurred in the year 2017.
The petitioners have not established the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.

Hence, it is deemed appropriate to fix his income notionally as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in consultation with Insurance Companies which will be Rs.11,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged 45 years at the time of the accident.
Hence, a multiplier of '14' is adopted as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in SARLA VERMA & ORS V. DELHI TRANSPORT CORP.& ANR reported in 2009(6) SCC 121.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA & ORS V. DELHI TRANSPORT CORP.& ANR reported in 2009(6) SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking the income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month, 25% has to be NC: 2023:KHC:33686 added to his income towards future prospects as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.
V. PRANAY SETHI reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.
Further, the deceased, who had three dependants at the time of his death 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, on the count of 'loss of dependency', the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.15,40,000/- (11,000x12x14+ 25% x 2/3).
5.
Petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards ;loss of estate and funeral expenses;.
6. Petitioners are all entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium and thus together are entitled to Rs.1,20,000/- (40,000x3) under this head.

7. The learned advocate for the petitioners submits that the enhanced compensation may be released in favour of petitioner No.1.
NC: 2023:KHC:33686 8.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.16,90,000/- as against Rs.12,00,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the petitioners are together entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.4,90,000/- over and above what has been awarded by the Tribunal (Rs.16,90,000 minus Rs.12,00,000/-).

Further, given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of Smt Kamalamma vs A P Rajenthiran on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101104110/
3 petition till realization.
